catalog_quote: The Seputan occupied the whole drainage of the Kacu River until they were removed some distance downstream by a government program in the early 1970s. They comprise three autonomous groups: upper Kacu, lower Kacu, and Penané. ... All these people became true swidden farmers by the turn of the twentieth century. Seputan language (some 500 speakers) is closely related to Aoheng, the main difference being its strong stress on the penultimate syllable.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (text layer of the Wayback/scholarhub PDF; HAL copy also on file). The quoted sentence is present verbatim at lines 268-270, between the running header '344 Wacana Vol. 16 No. 2 (2015)' and the p.345 header, i.e. on p.344 as stated: 'All these people became true swidden farmers by the turn of the twentieth century. Seputan language (some 500 speakers) is closely related to Aoheng, the main difference being its strong stress on the penultimate syllable.' The same sentence is in the HAL deposit PDF (extracted text). I read the whole MSP section (pp.343-350): the 'Müller-Schwaner Punan Languages' part gives Aoheng/Kerého/Hovongan/Bukat consonant tables, the Aoheng 8-vowel system…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Seputan (one of the two varieties under aohe1237) has strong stress on the penultimate syllable; this is presented as the main feature distinguishing Seputan from the otherwise near-identical Aoheng, which implies Aoheng lacks strong penultimate stress, but the source never says where Aoheng stress falls.
new_statements.exceptions: None; single-sentence remark, no discussion of schwa syllables, clitics or loans.
new_statements.domain_note: Impressionistic word-level remark based on Sellato's own field data (all data collected by Sellato, 1970s-80s); no phrase/citation-form distinction made. Applies to the Seputan variety only; Aoheng proper (the variety whose consonant and vowel inventories the article tabulates) receives no stress statement.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement concerns the Seputan variety (upper Kacu / Penane, upper Mahakam), which Glottolog 5.1 subsumes with Aoheng (Penihing) under the language-level code aohe1237 'Aoheng-Seputan' (no separate dialect codes listed). For Aoheng proper the source gives segment inventories but no stress locus; it only implies Aoheng lacks the 'strong' penultimate stress of Seputan. A catalog entry should be labelled 'Seputan variety; Aoheng unstated'.

sources.note: p.344: Seputan is closely related to Aoheng, 'the main difference being its strong stress on the penultimate syllable'. The phonology section (pp.345-348) gives Aoheng, Kereho, Hovongan, Bukat consonant tables and the Aoheng 8-vowel system but says nothing further about stress; where Aoheng stress falls is not stated.
